extracted.intended_audience: General readers, students, and researchers interested in Octavia E. Butler, her works, and their adaptations
extracted.subtask_description: A Wikipedia-style encyclopedic article summarizing Octavia E. Butler's life, bibliography, awards, adaptations, and critical reception. Intended to provide an overview and reference material about the author and her works.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visual differentiation of time periods in graphic adaptations
rubrics_metrics.description: To visually differentiate the time periods in which Butler set the story, Jennings used muted colors for the present and vibrant ones for the past to demonstrate how the remnants and relevance of slavery are still with us.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use divergent color palettes to signal different temporal settings and to reinforce thematic connections — e.g., muted tones for the contemporary/present scenes and vibrant colors for past sequences; this can underscore thematic continuity (such as the ongoing relevance of slavery) when adapting prose to graphic form. Example: Damian Duffy and John Jennings' graphic-novel adaptation of Kindred applied this technique.
